methodology: 5000-resample percentile bootstrap across independent target sessions. Target labels confined to scoring. Frequency uses offline unlabeled per-session counts and known popularity ordering; traffic profiles on the first half of sessions of each trial and tests on disjoint remaining sessions. Binary balanced-accuracy chance is 0.5; frequency accuracy must be compared with its imbalanced majority baseline.
limitations: Simplified component attacks on synthetic workloads. No reproduction of published inference algorithms. No joint-transcript, scheduler, inter-arrival, cold-start, cache, adversarial-failure or full-pipeline classifier evaluation. Application payload lengths and local component durations are not TCP packet sizes. Near-chance performance is not a security proof. Frequency scores are hard ranking decisions, not calibrated confidence.
